title: Library of Alexandria
summary: The Library of Alexandria was a Ptolemaic institution in Alexandria, Egypt, said to be in the Royal Quarter and founded in the 3rd century BCE under Ptolemy I or II. Its exact site, size and holdings are uncertain, and how it ended is debated: the fire of 48 BCE, the Serapeum's destruction in 391 CE and gradual decline are all proposed, while the story of its burning in the Arab conquest is judged a myth.

uncertainty.note: Start: National Geographic says that around 295 BC Ptolemy I tasked Demetrius with building the collection and that it opened between 284 and 246 BC, so the start range allows 50 years later. End: no single destruction date is established; 48 or 47 BCE (Caesar's fire) is the earliest candidate, and Roger Bagnall, as cited by the Open University, suggests large-scale destruction in the early 270s CE, so the end range runs about 320 years later. Decline may have been gradual.

reviewer_note: No surviving structure, so no model. The pin is the centre of modern Alexandria, not the library: EBSCO says it was "somewhere in the Royal Quarter" and Open University notes ignorance of its position and layout, so uncertainty_km is 5. Founder is unclear (Ptolemy I or II). The when range is wide on purpose: the end is debated and may be gradual. No scroll counts used because the sources give only unreliable ancient figures.
